A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-classifier-based continual personalization work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, generated images, ablations, and runtime measurements across four datasets, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative multi-concept results, Stable Diffusion v2.0 comparisons, and further diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The DC-based EWC and DSC procedures, teacher sampling, losses, and LoRA workflow remain unchanged. New Algorithm 4 summarizes the existing procedure; Appendix A expands token-training explanations rather than introducing a component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Custom Concept, Google Landmarks v2, Textual Inversion objects, and CelebA, including long sequences and multi-concept generation. Stable Diffusion v2.0 adds a model configuration, not new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Custom Diffusion joins the multi-concept comparison in v3 Figure 16b and Table 6; v1 Figure 17b compared only C-LoRA and the proposed method. The principal single-concept comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation with Stable Diffusion v2.0 on two benchmarks and a quantitative multi-concept protocol: 400 images per prompt, scored against individual-concept references and averaged across concepts and prompts. Section 4 also changes the stated EWC concept count from 3 to 5, resolving a conflict with v1's existing ablation text; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses expand substantially: v3 tests backbone compatibility, FIM eigenvalues across consolidation durations (Figure 18), sampled-timestep distributions (Figure 21), joint EWC/DSC loss-weight sensitivity (Figure 26), and runtime versus concept count (Table 10). Earlier individual-parameter ablations, teacher-design checks, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging remains the reporting practice, including in the new Stable Diffusion v2.0 tables. Neither version reports performance confidence intervals or significance tests. The added timestep distributions and FIM sweeps are diagnostics rather than a new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results in Tables 6–8 and 10 and the new diagnostic figures. For example, Table 6 reports multi-concept CLIP I2I scores of 64.53 for the proposed method, 52.45 for C-LoRA, and 48.50 for Custom Diffusion; v1 supplied only qualitative examples. Most earlier numerical entries remain, while Table 3 corrects metric assignments and retained tables change the stated KID scale from 10^3 to 10^5.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and Appendix I complexity derivations are retained, with no new theorem or proof. Equation 5 makes the expectation over inputs explicit, consistent with the existing sample-wise algorithm, rather than introducing substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The main continual-personalization, performance, and resource claims remain. The revised conclusion adds an explicit priority claim for reinforcing pretrained class-specific diffusion knowledge through fine-tuning to improve downstream generation, strengthening the stated novelty.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new consolidation-duration analysis as saturation of FIM information beyond 200 iterations and qualifies runtime overhead by concept count. Existing discussions of prompt sensitivity, pretrained-concept interference, and visual failure cases remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link, an overall workflow summary, and fuller instructions for learning and freezing concept-token embeddings. Hardware, learning rates, LoRA rank, and standard training budgets are retained; the link alone does not establish code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Jha et al. (2020), Jha et al. (2023), and Dieleman's diffusion-distillation discussion. Its conclusion makes the novelty positioning against test-time diffusion classification more explicit, without broadly restructuring the related-work argument.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. Changes include the rewritten conclusion, expanded token-training explanation, acknowledgements, author/header updates, and incorporation of the long-sequence subsection into the main results section. These are localized edits rather than an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation gains four result tables and three analysis figures. v3 also adds a Custom Diffusion column to the multi-concept montage, merges the two taskwise-performance figures, and relocates the long-sequence plot to the appendix. Table revisions correct TI column alignment and metric-direction arrows and change KID scale labels.

improvement.justification: v3 improves readability and evidential support through corrected table alignment and metric directions, clearer workflow documentation, and additional backbone and quantitative multi-concept comparisons. The gains are limited by sparse explanation of some new experiments and retained inconsistencies: the claimed 3.19-point backward-transfer improvement still conflicts with Table 1's change from -99.34 to -102.53 under the higher-is-better definition.
